title: Guru Gobind Singh’s Sacrifice for the Panth

blocks.text: The argument turns to the tenth Guru: as Mughal clerics and rulers forgot older bonds and set themselves against the Gurus, Guru Gobind Singh answered in anger and founded the Panth to confront tyranny directly. (2–3)
The passage frames the Guru’s loss of his four sons not as defeat but as a deliberate offering made for the life of the Panth, and asks why lineage was not preserved alongside mission. (3–4)

In reply, the poet compares Guru Gobind Singh with earlier founders and prophets, insisting that for the sake of the Panth he accepted blame, sacrifice, and conflict so that Sikhs might be preserved and the wicked destroyed. (5–9)
